try { const data=JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync('/data/alerts-cache.json','utf8'));if(!Array.isArray(data.rows)||!Array.isArray(data.seen))throw new Error('Invalid alert cache');context.set('rows',data.rows.slice(0,500));context.set('seen',data.seen.slice(-10000));context.set('storageError','');}
catch(e){if(e.code!=='ENOENT'){node.warn('Cannot restore alert cache: '+e.message);context.set('storageError','Alert history could not be restored: '+e.message);}}

HTTP: API_URL (http://central:8000), GET devices/history/processes/rules; PUT full rule list.
Alert cache: /data/alerts-cache.json (500 displayed records and 10000 duplicate IDs); atomic snapshot writes.
Saved flows are mounted at nodered/data/flows.json. Do not commit runtime cache, credentials, node_modules or collected device history.
Recovery checks: retained startup state, disk restore in fresh Function context, MQTT offline queuing, duplicate replay, API errors, independent browser selections, and rule version conflict.
Actual Docker container restart/build and real Raspberry Pi/network tests require Docker or hardware access.
